31.EMPLOYEEBENEFITS
(A)NUMBEROFEMPLOYEES
As at 3O June 2O13 the consolidated entity employed 7,O43 full-time employees (2O12: 8,416) and 1,384 part-time and casual
employees (2O12: 1.748). This inclucles 1.813 (2O12: 2,094) full-time employees ancl 285 (20O12: 31O) part-time and casual employees
in New Zealand.
(B)EMPLOYEESHAREPLANS
The Company had three employee share plans curing the period. The terms of each plan are set out below:
1. FAIRFAX EXEMPT EMPLOYEE SHARE PLAN
This plan is open to all Australian employees with at least twelve months service with the consolidated entity in Australia, whose
adjusted taxable income is $18O,OOO per annum or less. Under this Plan, participants may salary sacrifice up to $1,OOO of pre
tax salary per annum for the purchase of issuec Fairfax shares at the market price on the open market of the ASx. The shares
are purchased by an independent trustee company on predetermined dates.
2. FAIRFAX DEFERRED EMPLOYEE SHARE PLAN
This plan is open to all Australian employees with at least twelve months service with the consolidated entity in Australia.
for the purchase of issued Fairfax shares at the market price on the open market of the ASX. The shares are purchased by an
independent trustee company on predetermined dates. Participants must nominate a lock' period of either 3. 5 or 7 years
cluring which their shares must remain in the plan, unless they leave the consolidated entity in Australia.
3. LONG TERM EQUITY BASEDINCENTIVE SCHEME
The long term incentive plan is available to certain permanent full-time and part-time employees of the consoliclated entity.
2008-2012FinancialYear
Under this plan, the cash value of a percentage of an eligible executive's annual total fixed remuneration will be in the form of
nominally allocated Fairfax shares, which are beneficially held in a trust. The shares will vest if the eligible employee remains
in employment three years from the date the nominal shares are allocated and certain performance hurdles are satisfied. lf
the allocation does not vest at the end of year three. a re-test of the performance hurdles occurs in the fourth year. There are
currently no cash settlement altermatives. Dividends on the allocated shares during the vesting period are paid directly to the
eligible employee and the Company does not have any recourse to dividends paid.
2013FinancialYear
 For 2o13. participants in the plan received an allocation of performance rights (rights) which allow the executive to acquire
unvested rights.
The number of rights to which a participant is entitled will depend on the participant's role anc responsibilities. Allocations are
set at a fixed percentage of the executive's fixec remuneration at the time they participate in the scheme. The value of the rights
at the time of allocation is determined by an independent external valuer.
